report.verdict: A genuinely strong top line — net sales SEK 29.2m (~$2.90m), +130% YoY and +38% QoQ with cash opex up only 6% QoQ — but the near-breakeven EBITDA is flattered by SEK 5.8m (~$0.58m) of capitalised development and the net loss by a SEK 1.7m (~$0.17m) non-cash FX gain; underlying EBITDA was SEK −6.6m (~$−0.66m) and free cash flow SEK −11.9m (~$−1.18m), roughly 3x the year-ago burn. The quarter closed with SEK 0.36m (~$0.04m) of cash and SEK −27.8m (~$−2.76m) of equity, forcing SEK 45.2m (~$4.50m) of directed issues at SEK 0.65 (32% dilution, ~SEK 23m net cash) — and the CFO resigned three days after the report. Shares +18% on the day; the real test is whether Q4 delivers the positive operating cash flow the board has pointed to.
summary: **Headline growth is real and accelerating**: net sales SEK 29.2m (~$2.90m), +130.4% YoY from SEK 12.7m (~$1.26m) and +38.4% QoQ from SEK 21.1m (~$2.10m); 9M net sales SEK 65.3m (~$6.50m), +94.4%. The sequential run is 10.2 → 12.7 → 15.1 → 15.1 → 21.1 → 29.2 over six quarters. There is no sell-side consensus; Gaming Intelligence and Inderes/MFN corroborate the company figures.

**Reported EBITDA near breakeven — but read the capitalisation line**: EBITDA SEK −0.8m (~$−0.08m) vs SEK −7.6m (~$−0.75m) a year ago and SEK −5.8m (~$−0.57m) in Q2; margin −2.7% vs −59.9%. 'Own work capitalised' was SEK 5.8m (~$0.58m), 20% of sales and 4x the year-ago SEK 1.4m. EBITDA before capitalisation was SEK −6.6m (~$−0.66m) (−22.7% margin) vs SEK −9.0m (~$−0.89m) YoY and SEK −12.7m (~$−1.26m) QoQ — a 48% sequential improvement, not breakeven.

**Net loss SEK −2.6m (~$−0.25m), EPS SEK −0.02 (~$−0.002)**, helped by a SEK +1.7m (~$+0.17m) non-cash FX gain on long-term intra-group receivables. Ex-FX the loss was SEK −4.2m (~$−0.42m) vs SEK −7.3m (~$−0.72m) in Q2 — the CEO's '65% improvement vs Q2' is ~42% on an underlying basis. EBIT SEK −3.6m (~$−0.36m) vs SEK −7.9m.

**Operating leverage is the bull case**: total cash opex (external + personnel + other) SEK 36.0m (~$3.58m), +6% QoQ against +38% revenue. Other external costs SEK 23.6m (~$2.35m) = 81% of sales (118% a year ago); personnel SEK 12.2m (~$1.22m) = 42% (53%). Team headcount incl. consultants fell to 74 at the report date from 87 at the Q2 report (−15%).

**Liquidity was at the wire**: cash SEK 0.36m (~$0.04m) at 30 Sep vs SEK 1.5m at June and SEK 7.3m at December. Q3 operating cash flow SEK −5.2m (~$−0.51m), investing SEK −6.7m (~$−0.67m), free cash flow SEK −11.9m (~$−1.18m) — ~3x the SEK −4.1m (~$−0.41m) burn of Q3-25 — funded by SEK 11.8m (~$1.17m) of new short-term loans drawn in the quarter.

**Cash burn rose YoY despite the better P&L**: 9M free cash flow SEK −30.9m (~$−3.08m) vs SEK −27.1m (~$−2.70m) in 9M-25, because investment in capitalised development nearly tripled to SEK 16.4m (~$1.64m) from SEK 6.1m (~$0.61m). Capitalisation shifts cost from EBITDA into the balance sheet (NBV SEK 21.7m, ~$2.16m, vs SEK 8.7m at December), and D&A is now ramping (SEK 2.8m in Q3 vs SEK 1.0m in Q2).

**Negative equity for a third straight quarter**: group equity SEK −27.8m (~$−2.76m), equity/share SEK −0.19, solvency 'neg.' (29.0% a year ago). Our reconstruction puts gross interest-bearing debt at ~SEK 41.6m (~$4.14m) and net debt ~SEK 41.2m (~$4.10m) at 30 Sep [analyst estimate]. The report says the October issue improves the company's ability to operate 'in accordance with applicable listing requirements' — a tacit admission of the squeeze.

**Expensive bridge financing**: the June bridge (~SEK 13m, ~$1.3m, from a group of investors) included ~EUR 1m (~SEK 11m, ~$1.1m) from 29% holder Denwena at 2.5% per month (~30% p.a.), unsecured, due 31 Dec 2026, approved as a related-party transaction at the 3 Aug EGM. It is being extinguished by set-off in the October placement.

**Recapitalisation (post-period) — the de facto guidance event**: 13/14 Oct directed issue of 56,564,703 shares at SEK 0.65 (~$0.065), a 17.7% discount to 30-day VWAP, raising ~SEK 36.8m (~$3.66m) gross from external professionals and existing holders incl. Denwena, Redén Trotting and Svea Bank (fully subscribed, 30 Oct); 2 Nov EGM approved a second 12,860,078-share 'Leo-circle' placement (~SEK 8.4m, ~$0.84m) to insiders incl. CEO Juha Kauppinen and board members Christoffer Hartmann (Denwena) and Robert Larsson (fully subscribed, 12 Nov). Gross SEK 45.2m (~$4.50m); per secondary summaries of the release ~SEK 19.2m (~$1.91m) is debt set-off and ~SEK 23.1m (~$2.30m) is expected net cash. Combined dilution 32.3%; share count 145.4m → 214.9m.

**EGM rejected the Svea Bank set-off**: shareholders voted down the board's proposed 3,604,283-share issue to settle Svea's remaining ~SEK 2.34m (~$0.23m) claim, which therefore stays on the balance sheet as debt.

**Pro-forma position [analyst estimate]**: equity ≈ +SEK 15m (~$1.5m) before Q4 losses; gross debt ≈ SEK 22m (~$2.2m); net debt ≈ zero at completion; market cap ≈ SEK 163m (~$16.2m) at SEK 0.76 on the enlarged count (vs SEK 97.2m, ~$9.7m, at the 30 Sep close of SEK 0.67). At the Q3 burn rate the net proceeds cover ~two quarters.

**Guidance: none numeric** — the report states the company makes no detailed revenue forecast. Qualitative: October 'continued to deliver healthy growth'; target of ~3 proprietary releases/month in Q4 (7 in Q3); Q4-26/Q1-27 roadmap published; FY2027 strategy being finalised; and, per secondary coverage of the 14 Oct release, the board sees good prospects for positive operating cash flow before end-2026 — demanding versus Q3 CFO of SEK −5.2m.

**Cost-transformation programme**: 14 Jul termination of the June-2025 strategic agreement with Denwena and the Aug-2024 game-development agreement with Degen Studios, which management says 'drove significant costs' without matching revenue; remaining collaboration capped at ~EUR 0.6m (~$0.7m); a SEK 4.4m (~$0.44m) sale of a game-production technology platform to Degen was proposed; milestone warrants at SEK 1.34 under the old deal fall away. Full savings guided to flow 'gradually over coming quarters'.

**Distribution and product KPIs**: 2,540+ live online casinos (+27% YoY, +10% QoQ) across ~30 regulated markets/50+ geographies; 7 releases in Q3, 24 YTD vs 18; direct integrations rising alongside aggregators (IGT Digital, EveryMatrix, BetConstruct, Games Global, 1X2, Light & Wonder, Playtech). No GGR, handle, actives, ARPU, product or geographic revenue split is disclosed; the eight-quarter 'total bets' chart is indexed only.

**Commercial newsflow was dense**: Entain expansion (8 Jul), evoke plc (23 Jul), Games Global global distribution (10 Aug), PlayWin/NHL-legends IP (20 Aug), Bally's Intralot multi-market (27 Aug), Playtech global (8 Sep), Loto-Québec (17 Sep); post-period Veikkaus (26 Oct) and Apollo Games/Czech Republic (17 Nov). Ontario launch showed 'strong early results'; a new third-party North American distribution set-up on better terms is promised 'shortly'. No deal has disclosed financial terms.

**Governance**: CFO Fredrik Geijer (joined Feb-26) resigned on 16 Nov, three days after the report; shares −6.1%. Denwena retains ~29% and a board seat (Hartmann) despite the commercial split, and bought into both placements. Both issues bypassed pre-emption rights. The report is unaudited and prepared under Swedish K3, not IFRS; capitalisation of development began only in Oct-2024.

**Working capital unwound in Q3**: ~SEK 4.7m (~$0.47m) outflow as trade payables fell to SEK 12.1m (~$1.20m) from SEK 14.7m and accrued liabilities to SEK 6.2m (~$0.62m) from SEK 11.3m. Payables remain ~3x the year-ago level (SEK 4.4m), so further normalisation could absorb part of the new cash.
**Share price**: +18.1% to SEK 0.76 (~$0.076) on 13 Nov; −6.1% to SEK 0.71 on 16 Nov (CFO exit); +5.9% to SEK 0.75 on 17 Nov (Czech deal). Q3-end close SEK 0.67 vs SEK 1.02 a year earlier (−34%).

**Thesis read-through**: with cash opex ~SEK 36m/quarter, ex-capitalisation EBITDA breakeven is roughly a SEK 36m (~$3.6m) quarterly-revenue event — plausibly Q1/Q2-27 if growth holds at +15–20% QoQ with flat costs. The recap buys about two quarters of runway at Q3 burn; the Q4 print (19 Feb 2027) — specifically operating cash flow and year-end cash — is the make-or-break data point, not revenue.

segments.name: Group operating business – B2B online-casino content (single reportable segment)
segments.headline: Revenue +130% YoY with opex +6% QoQ delivers real operating leverage; but capitalisation (20% of sales) and a non-cash FX gain make the reported EBITDA/net-loss look two to three times better than the underlying.
narrative: They reported net sales of SEK 29.2m (~$2.90m) for the quarter, +130% YoY from SEK 12.7m (~$1.26m) and +38% QoQ from SEK 21.1m (~$2.10m), extending a sequence that has run 10.2 → 12.7 → 15.1 → 15.1 → 21.1 → 29.2 over the last six quarters; 9M sales were SEK 65.3m (~$6.50m), +94%. Management attributes the growth to a broadening distribution footprint — live online casinos at 2,540+ versus 2,310+ at June and 2,000+ a year ago — a higher release cadence (seven proprietary titles in the quarter, 24 year-to-date versus 18), and a rising share of direct operator integrations alongside the aggregators (IGT Digital, EveryMatrix, BetConstruct, Games Global, 1X2, Light & Wonder, Playtech). The company is a pure supplier, so there is no sportsbook handle or net margin to analyse, and nothing is disclosed on GGR, wagers, active players, ARPU, or revenue by product or geography; the report's eight-quarter 'total bets' chart is indexed with no absolute figures and the player-count chart is not quantified in the text. The only sub-split is the parent company's unconsolidated net sales of SEK 12.5m (~$1.24m), +62% YoY, with the balance flowing through the Malta subsidiary. Gaming Intelligence's SEK 29.2m / ~EUR 2.6m and Inderes/MFN's 130.4% match the company figures.

The P&L improvement is real but smaller than the headline. Reported EBITDA was SEK −0.8m (~$−0.08m), from SEK −7.6m (~$−0.75m) a year ago and SEK −5.8m (~$−0.57m) in Q2, a margin of −2.7% against −59.9%. But the group capitalises development: 'own work capitalised' was SEK 5.8m (~$0.58m) in the quarter — 20% of net sales — versus SEK 1.4m a year ago and SEK 6.9m in Q2. Stripping that out, EBITDA before capitalisation was SEK −6.6m (~$−0.66m) against SEK −9.0m (~$−0.89m) in Q3-25 and SEK −12.7m (~$−1.26m) in Q2: a 48% sequential improvement, not the near-breakeven the headline suggests. Other external costs rose 58% YoY to SEK 23.6m (~$2.35m) but were flat QoQ (+2.5%) and fell to 81% of sales from 118%; personnel costs rose 84% YoY and 14% QoQ to SEK 12.2m (~$1.22m), 42% of sales from 53%. Total cash opex was SEK 36.0m (~$3.58m), +6% QoQ, so Q3 operating leverage came entirely from the top line. The 74 team members at the report date (36 of them consultants, booked in external costs) compare with 87 at the Q2 report, a 15% reduction following the 14 July termination of the Denwena/Degen Studios agreements, which management says had 'driven significant costs' without commensurate revenue; the remaining collaboration is capped at ~EUR 0.6m (~$0.7m), a SEK 4.4m (~$0.44m) technology-platform sale to Degen was proposed, and the full cost benefit is guided to come through gradually.

Below EBITDA, D&A stepped up to SEK 2.8m (~$0.28m) from SEK 1.0m in Q2 as the capitalised development balance (SEK 21.7m, ~$2.16m, up from SEK 8.7m at December) begins to amortise — a drag that will grow for several quarters. EBIT was SEK −3.6m (~$−0.36m) versus SEK −7.9m (~$−0.79m). A SEK +1.7m (~$+0.17m) non-cash FX gain on long-term intra-group receivables and SEK 0.6m of interest took the net loss to SEK −2.6m (~$−0.25m), EPS SEK −0.02 (~$−0.002); excluding the FX swing the loss was SEK −4.2m (~$−0.42m) versus SEK −7.3m (~$−0.72m) in Q2 (−42%) and SEK −8.3m (~$−0.83m) a year ago. The CEO letter's '65% improvement vs Q2' is therefore about 42% underlying. Management emphasises the growth rate, the net-loss improvement and the partnership list; it does not mention in the letter that cash ended the quarter at SEK 0.36m (~$0.04m), that equity is negative, or that SEK 11.8m (~$1.17m) of short-term bridge money was drawn in the quarter.

The commercial newsflow was dense: an expanded Entain partnership (8 Jul), evoke plc (23 Jul), a global distribution agreement with Games Global (10 Aug), a PlayWin partnership giving access to NHL-legend IP for North America (20 Aug), Bally's Intralot multi-market (27 Aug), a global Playtech agreement (8 Sep) and Loto-Québec (17 Sep), followed post-period by Finland's monopoly operator Veikkaus (26 Oct) and Apollo Games for the Czech Republic (17 Nov). Management flagged 'strong early results' from the Ontario launch and says it is setting up a new third-party distribution arrangement for North America on more favourable terms, with details promised shortly, aimed at faster access to regulated US/Canadian markets and better margins; it also cites 'several promising discussions with major US operators'. State lotteries and government-controlled operators are an explicit strategic segment. None of these agreements come with disclosed financial terms, and the company's stated IR policy is to announce only deals it judges commercially or strategically significant — so the announced list is a floor on activity but tells us nothing about revenue concentration, which is also undisclosed.

There is no numeric guidance — the report explicitly says the company makes no detailed revenue forecast given continuous launches and integrations. Qualitatively: October 'continued to deliver healthy growth'; the release-cadence target is an average of three proprietary games per month in Q4 (versus seven in Q3 and ten in Q2); a Q4-26/Q1-27 product roadmap is published; and the FY2027 strategy is being finalised with a focus on existing partnerships and 'progress towards profitability'. The 14 Oct financing release, per secondary coverage, indicated the board sees good prospects for positive operating cash flow before end-2026 — ambitious given Q3 operating cash flow of SEK −5.2m (~$−0.51m), and it is worth noting the difference between operating cash flow (before capitalised development) and free cash flow, which would remain negative even if that target is met.

segments.name: Balance sheet, cash flow & recapitalisation (deep dive)
segments.headline: SEK 0.36m of cash and SEK −27.8m of equity at 30 Sep, financed by 2.5%-a-month bridge money; fixed post-period with SEK 45.2m of directed issues at SEK 0.65 (32% dilution, ~SEK 23m net cash) — roughly two quarters of runway at the Q3 burn rate.
narrative: Cash and solvency were the quarter's real story, and management did not lead with them. Cash at 30 September 2026 was SEK 0.36m (~$0.04m), down from SEK 1.5m (~$0.15m) at June and SEK 7.3m (~$0.72m) at December, after a quarter in which operating cash flow was SEK −5.2m (~$−0.51m), investment in capitalised development roughly SEK −7.0m (net investing SEK −6.7m, ~$−0.67m) and free cash flow SEK −11.9m (~$−1.18m) — nearly three times the SEK −4.1m (~$−0.41m) burn of Q3-25. The gap was bridged by SEK 11.8m (~$1.17m) of new short-term borrowings drawn in the quarter (9M short-term loans raised SEK 12.8m), i.e. the June bridge facility of ~SEK 13m (~$1.3m) from a group of investors, of which ~EUR 1m (~SEK 11m, ~$1.1m) from 29% shareholder Denwena at 2.5% per month, unsecured, due 31 December 2026 and approved as a related-party transaction at the 3 August EGM. For the nine months, free cash flow was SEK −30.9m (~$−3.08m) versus SEK −27.1m (~$−2.70m) in 9M-25: despite the better P&L, cash burn increased YoY because capitalised development spend nearly tripled (SEK 16.4m vs 6.1m).

Working capital reversed in Q3. The H1 inflow of SEK +8.7m — largely stretched payables and accruals — partially unwound, with trade payables down to SEK 12.1m (~$1.20m) from SEK 14.7m and accrued liabilities to SEK 6.2m (~$0.62m) from SEK 11.3m, a ~SEK 4.7m (~$0.47m) outflow; payables are still ~3x the year-ago SEK 4.4m, so further normalisation is likely. Trade receivables were SEK 6.9m (~$0.69m), roughly 22 days of sales, with a further SEK 8.7m (~$0.87m) in prepaid expenses and accrued income. Group equity was SEK −27.8m (~$−2.76m), equity per share SEK −0.19, solvency 'neg.' for the third consecutive quarter against +29.0% a year earlier; only the parent's SEK 140m (~$13.9m) intra-group receivable keeps the parent's own equity positive at SEK 99.5m (~$9.9m), which is also where the quarter's FX 'gain' arises. Our reconstruction of gross interest-bearing debt at 30 September is ~SEK 41.6m (~$4.14m) — bank SEK 2.1m, other long-term investor loans SEK 26.7m (~$2.66m) and ~SEK 12.8m of short-term loans within other current liabilities — giving net debt of ~SEK 41.2m (~$4.10m) versus ~SEK 9.7m at December [analyst estimate; the company publishes no net-debt figure]. Unrecognised tax losses were SEK 174.2m (~$17.3m) at end-2025.

The fix came after period-end. On 13/14 October the board, using the AGM authorisation, placed 56,564,703 shares at SEK 0.65 (~$0.065) — a 17.7% discount to the 30-day VWAP and below the SEK 0.67 quarter-end price — for ~SEK 36.8m (~$3.66m) with external professional investors and existing holders including Denwena, Redén Trotting and Svea Bank (fully subscribed, confirmed 30 Oct), and the 2 November EGM approved a second 12,860,078-share placement (~SEK 8.4m, ~$0.84m) to the 'Leo circle' of insiders including CEO Juha Kauppinen, board members Christoffer Hartmann (Denwena's representative) and Robert Larsson, and others (fully subscribed, 12 Nov). Gross proceeds are SEK 45.2m (~$4.50m), of which — per secondary summaries of the 14 Oct release that we could not open directly — ~SEK 19.2m (~$1.91m) is settled by set-off of loans, including the Denwena bridge, leaving ~SEK 23.1m (~$2.30m) of expected net cash after costs. The EGM rejected the board's proposal for a further 3,604,283-share set-off issue to Svea Bank for its remaining ~SEK 2.34m (~$0.23m) claim, which therefore stays as debt. The share count rises 47.7% to 214.9m; combined dilution 32.3%.

Pro forma, equity moves from SEK −27.8m to roughly +SEK 15m (~$1.5m) before Q4 losses and gross debt falls to ~SEK 22m (~$2.2m), with net debt around zero at completion [analyst estimates]; at SEK 0.76 the market capitalisation is ~SEK 163m (~$16.2m) on the enlarged share count. Management frames the issue as providing 'greater financial stability' and improving the ability to meet 'applicable listing requirements' — an acknowledgment that the working-capital position was at the edge of Nasdaq First North's requirements — and says ongoing financing costs are 'clearly reduced', which is credible given the 2.5%-a-month bridge is gone. With Q3 free cash flow at SEK −11.9m, ~SEK 23m of net cash is roughly two quarters of burn at the current rate, so runway depends on the promised swing to positive operating cash flow by year-end and on capitalised development not growing further. Three days after the report the CFO, in the role only since February, resigned (shares −6.1% on the day) with recruitment of a successor starting immediately — unhelpful timing for a company whose next test is its first clean balance sheet in two years and whose auditors have not reviewed this report.

blocks.heading: Cash and burn
blocks.takeaway: Cash fell to SEK 0.36m (~$0.04m) at 30 September after free cash flow of SEK −11.9m (~$−1.18m), nearly three times the Q3-25 burn, bridged by SEK 11.8m of short-term loans.
points: Cash down from SEK 1.5m (~$0.15m) at June and SEK 7.3m (~$0.72m) at December; management did not lead with this.
Operating cash flow SEK −5.2m (~$−0.51m); capitalised development roughly SEK −7.0m (net investing SEK −6.7m, ~$−0.67m); Q3-25 burn SEK −4.1m (~$−0.41m).
June bridge facility ~SEK 13m (~$1.3m), including ~EUR 1m (~SEK 11m, ~$1.1m) from 29% shareholder Denwena at 2.5% per month, unsecured, due 31 December 2026, approved at 3 August EGM.
9M free cash flow SEK −30.9m (~$−3.08m) versus SEK −27.1m (~$−2.70m) as capitalised development nearly tripled (SEK 16.4m vs 6.1m).

blocks.heading: Working capital and solvency
blocks.takeaway: H1's SEK +8.7m working-capital inflow partially unwound (~SEK 4.7m outflow); equity was SEK −27.8m (~$−2.76m), solvency negative for a third consecutive quarter.
points: Trade payables down to SEK 12.1m (~$1.20m) from SEK 14.7m, accrued liabilities to SEK 6.2m (~$0.62m) from SEK 11.3m; payables still ~3x year-ago SEK 4.4m, further normalisation likely.
Trade receivables SEK 6.9m (~$0.69m), roughly 22 days of sales; SEK 8.7m (~$0.87m) prepaid expenses and accrued income.
Equity per share SEK −0.19 versus solvency +29.0% a year earlier; parent's SEK 140m (~$13.9m) intra-group receivable keeps parent equity positive at SEK 99.5m (~$9.9m), source of the FX 'gain'.
Reconstructed gross interest-bearing debt ~SEK 41.6m (~$4.14m): bank SEK 2.1m, investor loans SEK 26.7m, ~SEK 12.8m short-term; net debt ~SEK 41.2m versus ~SEK 9.7m at December [analyst estimate].
Unrecognised tax losses SEK 174.2m (~$17.3m) at end-2025.

blocks.heading: Post-period recapitalisation
blocks.takeaway: Directed issues of 69.4m shares at SEK 0.65 raised SEK 45.2m gross (~SEK 23.1m net cash after ~SEK 19.2m loan set-off), with 32.3% combined dilution.
points: 13/14 October: 56,564,703 shares at SEK 0.65 (~$0.065), a 17.7% discount to 30-day VWAP and below SEK 0.67 quarter-end price, for ~SEK 36.8m (~$3.66m); investors include Denwena, Redén Trotting, Svea Bank; confirmed 30 Oct.
2 November EGM approved 12,860,078-share placement (~SEK 8.4m, ~$0.84m) to the 'Leo circle' including CEO Juha Kauppinen, Christoffer Hartmann and Robert Larsson; fully subscribed 12 Nov.
Set-off of ~SEK 19.2m (~$1.91m) including Denwena bridge, per secondary summaries of the 14 Oct release not opened directly; net cash ~SEK 23.1m (~$2.30m).
EGM rejected a further 3,604,283-share set-off issue to Svea Bank for its ~SEK 2.34m (~$0.23m) claim, which stays as debt.
Share count rises 47.7% to 214.9m.

blocks.heading: Pro forma and runway
blocks.takeaway: Pro forma equity ~+SEK 15m and net debt around zero, but ~SEK 23m net cash is roughly two quarters of burn at Q3's SEK −11.9m free cash flow.
points: Gross debt falls to ~SEK 22m (~$2.2m) [analyst estimates]; at SEK 0.76 market capitalisation ~SEK 163m (~$16.2m) on enlarged share count.
Management cites 'greater financial stability' and ability to meet 'applicable listing requirements', acknowledging working capital was at the edge of Nasdaq First North's requirements.
Financing costs 'clearly reduced', credible as the 2.5%-a-month bridge is gone.
Runway depends on the promised swing to positive operating cash flow by year-end and capitalised development not growing further.

blocks.heading: CFO resignation
blocks.takeaway: The CFO, in role only since February, resigned three days after the report (shares −6.1%), unhelpful timing ahead of the first clean balance sheet in two years.
points: Recruitment of a successor starts immediately.
Auditors have not reviewed this report.

highlights.text: **Growth is accelerating, not decelerating**: net sales SEK 29.2m (~$2.90m), +130% YoY and +38% QoQ, the sixth consecutive quarter of sequential growth; 9M +94% to SEK 65.3m (~$6.50m). Management says October continued to grow.

**Genuine operating leverage**: total cash opex SEK 36.0m (~$3.58m) rose only 6% QoQ against +38% revenue; external costs fell to 81% of sales (118% LY) and personnel to 42% (53%). EBITDA ex-capitalisation improved 48% QoQ to SEK −6.6m (~$−0.66m).

**Distribution breadth is compounding**: 2,540+ live casinos (+27% YoY), 24 releases YTD (vs 18), and tier-1 agreements in one quarter — Entain, evoke, Games Global, Bally's Intralot, Playtech, Loto-Québec — plus Veikkaus and Apollo Games (Czech) post-period; the state-lottery/monopoly channel is a differentiated route to regulated markets.

**Cost driver removed**: termination of the Denwena/Degen Studios agreements (14 Jul) cut team headcount from 87 to 74 (−15%), capped remaining collaboration at ~EUR 0.6m (~$0.7m), and eliminated the milestone-warrant dilution overhang at SEK 1.34; management guides further savings to flow gradually.

**Recapitalisation done, with insiders and the largest holder participating**: SEK 45.2m (~$4.50m) gross at SEK 0.65 (~$0.065) fully subscribed across both placements, extinguishing the 2.5%-a-month bridge via ~SEK 19.2m (~$1.91m) set-off and restoring positive pro-forma equity (~SEK +15m, ~$1.5m, analyst est.).

**North America optionality**: Ontario launch showed 'strong early results', Loto-Québec gives direct access to the regulated Québec market, and a new third-party US/Canada distribution structure on better terms is promised 'shortly'.

lowlights.text: **The quarter ended with SEK 0.36m (~$0.04m) of cash and SEK −27.8m (~$−2.76m) of equity** — solvency negative for a third quarter — kept afloat only by SEK 11.8m (~$1.17m) of short-term bridge loans drawn in Q3, part of it from the 29% shareholder at 2.5% per month. Management's letter does not mention any of this.

**Quality of earnings**: SEK 5.8m (~$0.58m) of capitalised development (20% of sales, 4x YoY) and a SEK +1.7m (~$+0.17m) non-cash FX gain flatter the P&L. EBITDA ex-capitalisation SEK −6.6m (~$−0.66m), net loss ex-FX SEK −4.2m (~$−0.42m); 9M free cash flow SEK −30.9m (~$−3.08m) was worse than 9M-25 (SEK −27.1m) despite the better P&L.

**Amortisation headwind building**: capitalised development NBV SEK 21.7m (~$2.16m), 2.5x December; Q3 D&A SEK 2.8m (~$0.28m) vs SEK 1.0m in Q2. The P&L will have to absorb this as the asset amortises, so EBIT will lag EBITDA for several quarters.

**32.3% dilution via two directed issues at a 17.7% VWAP discount with no pre-emption rights**, with insiders (CEO, board members) and Denwena — whose commercial deal the company had just terminated for driving costs without revenue — among the subscribers; the EGM pushed back by rejecting the Svea Bank set-off, leaving that ~SEK 2.34m (~$0.23m) claim as debt.

**CFO Fredrik Geijer resigned on 16 Nov after nine months**, three days after the report and in the middle of a recapitalisation; shares −6.1%. The report is unaudited and prepared under Swedish K3 rather than IFRS.

**Disclosure is thin for a 130%-growth story**: no GGR, wagers, active players, ARPU, product or geographic revenue split, no customer/aggregator concentration, no numeric guidance, and the accounting treatment of the SEK 4.4m (~$0.44m) platform sale to Degen Studios is not visible in the Q3 statements [unverified] — if any of it sits in net sales, underlying growth is overstated.

**Working-capital unwind**: ~SEK 4.7m (~$0.47m) outflow in Q3 as stretched payables (SEK 14.7m → 12.1m) and accruals (SEK 11.3m → 6.2m) came down; payables remain ~3x the year-ago level, so a further portion of the new cash is likely to go to creditors rather than growth.

forecast.intro: There is no formal numeric guidance to bridge — the company explicitly declines to forecast revenue. What changed between Q2 and Q3 is the financial framing, and it was driven entirely by the group's single operating business: at Q2 (14 Aug) the stance was 'liquidity strengthened by a ~SEK 13m bridge loan' with Denwena's EUR 1m tranche at 2.5%/month due 31 Dec 2026 and a solvency-negative balance sheet; by Q3 (13 Nov) the bridge has been converted into equity through SEK 45.2m (~$4.50m) of directed issues at SEK 0.65, ~SEK 19.2m (~$1.91m) of debt is set off, ~SEK 23.1m (~$2.30m) of net cash is expected, the share count rises to 214.9m, and the board (per secondary coverage of the 14 Oct release) has pointed to positive operating cash flow before end-2026. The moving parts are (i) revenue momentum — October 'healthy growth' and a 3-releases-a-month cadence; (ii) cost base — Denwena/Degen savings still flowing through, team already down to 74; (iii) capitalisation — SEK 5.8m/quarter that sits below operating cash flow but above free cash flow; and (iv) working-capital normalisation.

forecast.view: **Revenue**: we model Q4-26 net sales of SEK 33–36m (~$3.3–3.6m), +15–25% QoQ, taking FY26 to ~SEK 99–101m (~$9.9–10.0m), roughly double FY25 — consistent with 'healthy growth' in October, the higher release cadence and new distribution going live (Veikkaus, Loto-Québec, Playtech, Games Global), but deliberately below the +38% Q3 step because Q3 likely absorbed a cluster of integrations and the 3-release target is below Q3's seven. **Margin**: with cash opex of ~SEK 36–37m/quarter (Denwena savings offset by growth hires), Q4 reported EBITDA should turn modestly positive (SEK +1m to +3m) if capitalisation stays ~SEK 6m, while EBITDA ex-capitalisation remains ~SEK −2m to −4m; breakeven on the honest measure is a ~SEK 36m-revenue event, plausibly Q1/Q2-27. FY26E reported EBITDA ≈ SEK −15m (~$−1.5m), net loss ≈ SEK −24m to −26m (~$−2.4 to −2.6m) with D&A rising toward SEK 3.5m/quarter. **Cash/leverage**: ~SEK 23m net proceeds against a Q3 free-cash-flow burn of SEK 11.9m implies a year-end cash balance of roughly SEK 12–17m if Q4 burn moderates to SEK 6–10m (working-capital unwind is the swing), and pro-forma net debt of ~SEK 6–10m (~$0.6–1.0m) by December versus ~SEK 41m at September — leverage direction is sharply down, but absolute liquidity remains thin and a further raise in H2-27 cannot be excluded unless ex-capitalisation EBITDA turns positive by Q2-27. **Swing factors**: (1) whether the board's 'positive operating cash flow before end-2026' is met and how it is defined; (2) capitalisation rate — any step-up flatters EBITDA but burns cash; (3) the North American distribution restructuring and timing of US operator launches; (4) payables normalisation; (5) CFO succession and audit of the FY26 accounts, including going-concern language. All figures above are analyst estimates, not company guidance.
watch: Q4-26 report (19 Feb 2027): operating cash flow vs the board's 'positive before end-2026' statement, year-end cash after the ~SEK 23m net proceeds, and whether Q4 free cash flow is better than SEK −6m.
Capitalised development as % of sales (20% in Q3) and the D&A run-rate — track EBITDA ex-capitalisation, not reported EBITDA.

Confirmation of the exact cash vs set-off split and issue costs in the Q4 cash-flow statement, plus whether the SEK 4.4m Degen platform sale was booked in revenue, other income or investing [unverified].
CFO appointment and the FY2026 annual report/auditor's report (going-concern and listing working-capital statements); the Q3 report is unaudited.
Details of the new North American third-party distribution deal and the first US operator go-lives; progress in Ontario/Québec and with Veikkaus.
Svea Bank's ~SEK 2.34m claim (set-off rejected by the EGM) and the remaining ~SEK 22m of investor loans — maturities and interest cost post-recapitalisation.
Denwena's ~29% stake and board representation after the commercial split; any further related-party transactions or selling.
Working capital: trade payables (SEK 12.1m) and accrued liabilities normalising toward year-ago levels would consume cash.
Any disclosure of GGR/wagers, player counts or customer concentration — the growth story currently rests on net sales and 'casinos live' alone.

report.sharePriceReaction: Shares +18.1% to SEK 0.76 (~$0.076) on 13 Nov 2026 (MFN price feed on the day of the release), from SEK 0.64 the prior close; then −6.1% to SEK 0.71 on 16 Nov on the CFO's resignation and +5.9% to SEK 0.75 on 17 Nov on the Apollo Games/Czech agreement. Quarter-end close was SEK 0.67 (~$0.067), −34% YoY vs SEK 1.02, giving a market cap of SEK 97.2m (~$9.7m) pre-placement; ~SEK 163m (~$16.2m) at SEK 0.76 on the enlarged 214.9m share count.
